distinguishing_features: Passive geometric flow-force redirection at the luer to convert axial compressive force into hoop stress
Structural prevention of kink buckling rather than inference/monitoring of occlusion via telemetry
Helical channel plus reinforced-tubing geometry that shortens effective unsupported length
No reliance on pressure-rise leading indicator for detection
parsed.objective_technical_problem: How to physically prevent kink-induced occlusion at the luer connection without adding instrumentation or changing user workflow.
parsed.viable_reason: The mechanism is physically implausible as written: an axial compressive load redirected into hoop stress at a short luer cannot raise the critical buckling force 16x, the stated E=10 MPa with I=0.01 mm^4 gives an implausibly tiny F_cr, and the 0.1-0.5 N occlusion forces are not supported by the flow/pressure pass criterion.
parsed.non_obvious_reason: None of the prior art addresses passive structural anti-kink geometry; all three are telemetry-based inference/monitoring schemes, so the geometric prevention approach is not an obvious application of the closest art.
